strings.path.title: Metal Rhythm
strings.path.goal: Play a tight palm-muted riff with power chords, gallops and a pedal tone, at tempo with a band and for a full minute.
strings.path.assumes: You can play eighth notes with a click at 80 BPM and fret a note on the low strings cleanly. An electric guitar with some distortion helps, but every Exercise works clean. The minutes listed are one pass through the material; expect to come back to each Step for days or weeks.
strings.path.gradingLimits: The app times each attack and counts the ones it heard. A two-note power chord is one attack: it is timed and counted, and its pitch is not checked. Palm muting and the direction of each stroke are taught here and cannot be heard apart, so they are yours to keep honest. Heavy distortion and compression blur where a note starts; for a graded take, turn the gain down to a crunch, or use the dry signal if your interface has one. Sixteenths above 150 BPM are close to the fastest the app will grade. None of this has been tried on a real guitar yet.
strings.path.skills.0: Eighth notes with a click at 80 BPM
strings.path.skills.1: Clean single notes on the low strings
strings.step.the-chug.title: The chug
strings.step.the-chug.goal: Play palm-muted eighth notes on the low E string in downstrokes, every one the same weight, and lift the mute for an accent.
strings.step.the-chug.why: The palm-muted downstroke is the sound of metal rhythm guitar. It is two skills at once: the picking hand mutes and plays in the same place, and the stroke only ever goes down, so the hand has to come back up between every note without being heard.
strings.step.the-chug.howTo.0: Rest the side of the picking hand on the strings right where they leave the bridge. Too far forward and the note dies; too far back and it rings. Find the spot where it thuds and still has a pitch.
strings.step.the-chug.howTo.1: Every note is a downstroke. Play from the wrist, small, and let the hand bounce back up by itself.
strings.step.the-chug.howTo.2: For an accent, lift the palm a little so the string rings, and bring it straight back.
strings.step.the-chug.payoff: A two-bar riff on the low E string that thuds evenly and opens up where you choose.
strings.exercise.the-chug.open-chug.title: Eight to the bar
strings.exercise.the-chug.open-chug.purpose: Palm-muted eighths on the open low E string, all downstrokes, with two fretted notes at the end of the second bar. The sound comes first: get the mute right before you worry about speed.
strings.exercise.the-chug.open-chug.howTo.0: Eighth notes, two to the click, all down. The last two notes are frets 3 and 5, muted like the rest.
strings.exercise.the-chug.open-chug.howTo.1: Listen to each note. They should all be as short and as loud as each other, like a machine.
strings.exercise.the-chug.open-chug.coachLine: I time every stroke and say how even they were. The mute and the direction of the strokes are for you to judge.
strings.exercise.the-chug.open-chug.selfCheck.0: Did the muted notes thud with a clear pitch, neither ringing open nor choked dead?
strings.exercise.the-chug.open-chug.selfCheck.1: Were they all downstrokes, to the last bar?
strings.exercise.the-chug.chug-and-note.title: Muted and open
strings.exercise.the-chug.chug-and-note.purpose: The chug with fretted notes let out of the mute: G, A and the Bb that makes it sound heavy. The palm has to lift and come back inside an eighth note.
strings.exercise.the-chug.chug-and-note.howTo.0: Mute the open E notes and let the fretted notes ring: lift the palm just enough as you play them.
strings.exercise.the-chug.chug-and-note.howTo.1: First finger on fret 3, third on fret 5, little finger on fret 6. All downstrokes.
strings.exercise.the-chug.chug-and-note.coachLin: After the take I'll say how even it was and whether the notes were the written ones.
strings.exercise.the-chug.chug-and-note.selfChec: Did the muted notes thud with a clear pitch, neither ringing open nor choked dead?
strings.exercise.the-chug.accent-open.title: Accents in threes
strings.exercise.the-chug.accent-open.purpose: The open E string throughout, with the mute lifted on every third eighth: 3 + 3 + 2. The accents make the riff, and the notes never change.
strings.exercise.the-chug.accent-open.howTo.0: Lift the palm for the accented notes and dig in a little more. Mute everything else.
strings.exercise.the-chug.accent-open.howTo.1: Count '1 2 3, 1 2 3, 1 2'. In bar 2 the last two accents are frets 3 and 5.
strings.exercise.the-chug.accent-open.coachLine: Accents are measured roughly: louder than the notes either side or not. With heavy gain they flatten out, so try this one with less.
Accents are measured roughly, as louder than the notes either side. Compression and high gain flatten them.
strings.step.power-chords.title: Power chords
strings.step.power-chords.goal: Play two-note power chords on the low strings, move them without a gap, and stop them dead.
strings.step.power-chords.why: A power chord is a root and the note a fifth above it, on two neighbouring strings. It has no major or minor in it, which is why it stays clear under distortion. The shape never changes, so the work is in moving it in time and in silencing it.
strings.step.power-chords.howTo.0: First finger on the root, third finger two frets up on the next string. For E, the low E string is open and the first finger takes fret 2 of the A string.
strings.step.power-chords.howTo.1: Let the first finger lie lightly across the higher strings so they can't ring, and hit only the two strings of the chord.
strings.step.power-chords.howTo.2: To stop a chord, relax the fretting fingers without lifting them off the strings, and lay the picking hand down at the same time.
strings.step.power-chords.payoff: Three chords, E, G and A, that move in time and stop as one.
strings.exercise.power-chords.two-note-chords.pu: Three power chords in quarter notes, two of each. Slow enough to land both fingers at once and hear both strings.
strings.exercise.power-chords.two-note-chords.ho: E: open low E and fret 2 on the A string. G: fret 3 and fret 5. A: fret 5 and fret 7. Downstrokes through both strings.
Move the hand as one shape. The fingers keep their spacing while the hand slides.
strings.exercise.power-chords.two-note-chords.co: A chord is one attack to me: I time it and count it, and I don't check its pitch.
strings.exercise.power-chords.two-note-chords.se: Did both strings of every chord sound, and no others?
strings.exercise.power-chords.chord-stops.title: Chords and stops
strings.exercise.power-chords.chord-stops.purpos: Eighth-note chords with rests between them. The silence has to be as tight as the chord, or the riff turns to mush.
Count '1 and, (2) and, (3) and 4, (and)'. Stop the strings with both hands on each rest.
All downstrokes. The hand keeps moving in eighths through the rests.
strings.exercise.power-chords.chord-stops.coachL: I time each chord. A sound in a rest counts as an extra note; strings left humming are for your ear.
strings.exercise.power-chords.chord-stops.selfCh: On a recording, do the stops sound silent, with nothing ringing through them?
strings.exercise.power-chords.moving-fifths.purp: E held for a beat, then G and A as eighths, a rest, and round again: a riff made of nothing but power chords.
strings.exercise.power-chords.moving-fifths.howT: The hand jumps from the open E shape to fret 3. Go early: leave the E chord a hair before the beat is over.
Keep the first and third fingers on their strings as the shape slides between G and A.
strings.exercise.power-chords.moving-fifths.coac: The jump from E to G is where a chord arrives late. I'll say how even it was.
strings.step.chug-and-chord.title: Chug against chord
strings.step.chug-and-chord.goal: Switch between muted single notes and ringing power chords inside one bar, all in downstrokes.
strings.step.chug-and-chord.why: This is the riff every heavy band plays: a muted low string chugging, and chords punching out of it. The picking hand has to change from one muted string to two open ones and back in an eighth note, and the contrast between the two is the whole effect.
strings.step.chug-and-chord.howTo.0: Muted notes: one string, palm down, small stroke. Chords: palm up, a bigger stroke through two strings.
strings.step.chug-and-chord.howTo.1: Keep the fretting hand's shape hovering over the next chord while the open string chugs.
strings.step.chug-and-chord.howTo.2: Loud chords, quiet chug. If they sound the same, exaggerate the difference until they don't.
strings.step.chug-and-chord.payoff: A riff that sounds like a record: chug, chug, chord.
strings.exercise.chug-and-chord.chug-chord.title: E chord out of the chug
strings.exercise.chug-and-chord.chug-chord.purpo: The 3 + 3 + 2 accents again, but each accent is now a ringing E power chord and the notes between are muted.
strings.exercise.chug-and-chord.chug-chord.howTo: First finger stays on fret 2 of the A string throughout. On the accents, lift the palm and strike both strings.
Bar 2 ends with G and A chords on the last two eighths.
strings.exercise.chug-and-chord.chug-chord.coach: I check that the chords were louder than the chug, roughly, and how even the time was.
strings.exercise.chug-and-chord.chug-chord.detec: Accents are measured roughly, as louder than the notes either side. Compression and high gain flatten them.
strings.exercise.chug-and-chord.chug-riff.title: Chords on the move
strings.exercise.chug-and-chord.chug-riff.purpos: Two muted notes, a G chord, two muted notes, an A chord: the chords change while the chug stays on the open string.
The fretting hand has two muted notes to get to each chord. Move during them.
The last chord of bar 2 is an E held for a beat. Let it ring.
strings.exercise.chug-and-chord.chug-riff.coachL: I time every attack, chug and chord alike, and say how even they were.
strings.exercise.chug-and-chord.chug-riff.selfCh: Did the muted notes thud with a clear pitch, neither ringing open nor choked dead?
strings.exercise.chug-and-chord.stop-riff.title: Chug, chord, stop
strings.exercise.chug-and-chord.stop-riff.purpos: The same idea with holes in it: a rest after the G chord and after the A. Three sounds now, muted, open and silent.
Count '1 and 2 and, (3) and 4, (and)'. Kill the chord with both hands on each rest.
Don't let the rest shorten. The muted note after it comes on the 'and', not before.
strings.exercise.chug-and-chord.stop-riff.coachL: The note after each rest is the one I'd look at: early is the usual mistake.
strings.exercise.chug-and-chord.stop-riff.selfCh: On a recording, do the stops sound silent, with nothing ringing through them?
strings.step.gallop.title: The gallop
strings.step.gallop.goal: Play the gallop, an eighth and two sixteenths, evenly on a muted string and against chords.
strings.step.gallop.why: The gallop is the rhythm of classic heavy metal. It is three strokes to a beat, down, down-up, and the trouble is the two short ones: they bunch up against the next beat unless the hand keeps a steady sixteenth-note swing underneath.
strings.step.gallop.howTo.0: Count '1, and a, 2, and a'. Down on the beat, then down-up on the 'and a'.
strings.step.gallop.howTo.1: The hand swings in sixteenths the whole time and misses the string once a beat, on the 'e'.
strings.step.gallop.howTo.2: Stay palm-muted and keep the strokes small. The gallop gets its sound from being tight, not loud.
strings.step.gallop.payoff: A galloping riff on the low E string that holds its shape as the tempo climbs.
strings.exercise.gallop.gallop-one.title: The gallop on one string
strings.exercise.gallop.gallop-one.purpose: Eight gallops on the muted low E string, the last two on frets 3 and 5. Nothing to think about except the three strokes.
strings.exercise.gallop.gallop-one.howTo.0: Down, down-up, on every beat. The long note is on the click.
strings.exercise.gallop.gallop-one.howTo.1: If the two short notes sound like one smeared note, slow down a rung until you can hear both.
strings.exercise.gallop.gallop-one.coachLine: I time all three notes of every beat and say how even they were. The strokes are yours to keep.
strings.exercise.gallop.gallop-one.detection.0: At this speed a real rig's input delay can push notes out of their matching window, which reads as late or missed. Evenness is the number to trust here, and only once the delay is calibrated.
strings.exercise.gallop.gallop-one.selfCheck.0: Did the muted notes thud with a clear pitch, neither ringing open nor choked dead?
strings.exercise.gallop.gallop-chords.title: A chord, then the gallop
strings.exercise.gallop.gallop-chords.purpose: A power chord on the first beat of each half bar, and the gallop carrying on underneath on the open string.
strings.exercise.gallop.gallop-chords.howTo.0: The chord takes the place of the gallop's long note: chord, then the two short muted notes, then a full gallop.
strings.exercise.gallop.gallop-chords.howTo.1: E, then G and A in the second bar. Lift the palm for the chord and drop it straight back.
strings.exercise.gallop.gallop-chords.coachLine: I time every attack and say how even they were. A chord's pitch is not something I check.
At this speed a real rig's input delay can push notes out of their matching window, which reads as late or missed. Evenness is the number to trust here, and only once the delay is calibrated.
strings.exercise.gallop.gallop-riff.title: A galloping riff
strings.exercise.gallop.gallop-riff.purpose: Two gallops, two open eighth notes that climb, and a gallop to answer; the second bar ends on a long note. E blues on one string.
strings.exercise.gallop.gallop-riff.howTo.0: The eighth notes on frets 3, 5 and 6 are open, not muted, and all downstrokes. Let the hand lean up a fret for the little finger on 6.
strings.exercise.gallop.gallop-riff.howTo.1: Keep the sixteenth-note swing going through the eighths, so the next gallop starts in time.
strings.exercise.gallop.gallop-riff.coachLine: After the take I'll say how even it was and whether the notes were the written ones.
strings.exercise.gallop.gallop-riff.detection.0: At this speed a real rig's input delay can push notes out of their matching window, which reads as late or missed. Evenness is the number to trust here, and only once the delay is calibrated.
strings.step.reverse-gallop.title: The reverse gallop
strings.step.reverse-gallop.goal: Play two sixteenths and an eighth, bursts of four sixteenths, and change between them and the gallop.
strings.step.reverse-gallop.why: Turn the gallop round and the short notes come first: down-up, down. It feels like a different rhythm and it trips players who learned the gallop as a reflex. Riffs mix the two, and a burst of four sixteenths between eighths, so each has to be a choice.
strings.step.reverse-gallop.howTo.0: Count '1 e and, 2 e and'. Down-up on the '1 e', down on the 'and'.
strings.step.reverse-gallop.howTo.1: The first short note is on the click. Don't let the pair fall early, before the beat.
strings.step.reverse-gallop.howTo.2: For four sixteenths and two eighths, count '1 e and a, 2 and': down-up-down-up, down, down.
strings.step.reverse-gallop.payoff: A riff with both gallops in it, played without having to think which is which.
strings.exercise.reverse-gallop.reverse-one.purp: Eight reverse gallops on the muted low E string, the last two on frets 3 and 5.
strings.exercise.reverse-gallop.reverse-one.howT: Down-up, down, on every beat. The hand misses the string on the 'a'.
Give the first note of each beat a little weight so you can hear where the beat is.
strings.exercise.reverse-gallop.reverse-one.coac: I time all three notes of every beat and say how even they were.
strings.exercise.reverse-gallop.reverse-one.dete: At this speed a real rig's input delay can push notes out of their matching window, which reads as late or missed. Evenness is the number to trust here, and only once the delay is calibrated.
strings.exercise.reverse-gallop.four-two.title: Four fast, two slow
strings.exercise.reverse-gallop.four-two.purpose: A beat of four muted sixteenths and a beat of two eighths, twice a bar. The eighths at the end of each bar are fretted and open.
strings.exercise.reverse-gallop.four-two.howTo.0: The sixteenths alternate, down-up-down-up. The eighths are both downstrokes.
strings.exercise.reverse-gallop.four-two.howTo.1: The eighths are exactly half the speed of the sixteenths. Players nearly always rush them.
strings.exercise.reverse-gallop.four-two.coachLi: After the take I'll say how even it was and whether the notes were the written ones.
strings.exercise.reverse-gallop.four-two.detecti: At this speed a real rig's input delay can push notes out of their matching window, which reads as late or missed. Evenness is the number to trust here, and only once the delay is calibrated.
strings.exercise.reverse-gallop.both-gallops.pur: A gallop, a reverse gallop, a gallop, and two open eighths; then the answer, ending on a long note.
strings.exercise.reverse-gallop.both-gallops.how: Say it first: '1, and a, 2 e and, 3, and a, 4 and'.
The hand swings in sixteenths from start to finish. Only which strokes touch the string changes.
strings.exercise.reverse-gallop.both-gallops.coa: This is the Step's test piece. I'll say how even it was and check the notes after the take.
strings.exercise.reverse-gallop.both-gallops.det: At this speed a real rig's input delay can push notes out of their matching window, which reads as late or missed. Evenness is the number to trust here, and only once the delay is calibrated.
strings.step.sixteenth-chug.title: Sixteenths, alternate picked
strings.step.sixteenth-chug.goal: Play a bar of continuous palm-muted sixteenths with strict down-up strokes, and put accents and fretted notes into it.
strings.step.sixteenth-chug.why: Past a certain tempo downstrokes run out and the hand has to alternate. Muted sixteenths on one string are where that starts: the upstroke has to be as heavy as the downstroke, under a palm mute, which is harder than it sounds because the pick meets the string from the other side.
strings.step.sixteenth-chug.howTo.0: Strict alternation: down on the beat and the 'and', up on the 'e' and the 'a'. Never two the same way.
strings.step.sixteenth-chug.howTo.1: Angle the pick a little so it slides through the string in both directions.
strings.step.sixteenth-chug.howTo.2: Accents are made by lifting the palm, on whichever stroke they fall.
strings.step.sixteenth-chug.payoff: A sixteenth-note riff with a melody poking out of the chug.
strings.exercise.sixteenth-chug.straight-sixteen: Two bars of muted sixteenths on the open low E string, with the mute lifted on the first note of every beat.
Down-up-down-up, four to the click. Lift the palm slightly on each beat's first note.
Listen to the upstrokes. If they are thinner than the downstrokes, slow down and even them out.
I check that the first note of each beat was louder, roughly, and how even the sixteenths were.
At this speed a real rig's input delay can push notes out of their matching window, which reads as late or missed. Evenness is the number to trust here, and only once the delay is calibrated.
Accents are measured roughly, as louder than the notes either side. Compression and high gain flatten them.
strings.exercise.sixteenth-chug.accent-threes.pu: The same sixteen notes with an accent every three: five accents a bar, and two of them fall on upstrokes.
strings.exercise.sixteenth-chug.accent-threes.ho: Count the sixteenths '1 2 3, 1 2 3, 1 2 3, 1 2 3, 1 2 3 4'. The picking never changes; only the palm does.
Tap your foot on the beat and let the accents pull against it.
strings.exercise.sixteenth-chug.accent-threes.co: The accents on the upstrokes are the test. The accent readout is rough, so trust your ear too.
strings.exercise.sixteenth-chug.accent-threes.de: At this speed a real rig's input delay can push notes out of their matching window, which reads as late or missed. Evenness is the number to trust here, and only once the delay is calibrated.
Accents are measured roughly, as louder than the notes either side. Compression and high gain flatten them.
strings.exercise.sixteenth-chug.sixteenth-riff.t: A melody out of the chug
strings.exercise.sixteenth-chug.sixteenth-riff.p: Sixteenths on the low E string where one note in four is fretted and open: G, A and Bb come up out of the muted pedal.
strings.exercise.sixteenth-chug.sixteenth-riff.h: First finger on fret 3, third on fret 5, little finger on fret 6. Lift the palm for the fretted notes.
Strict down-up. Nearly every fretted note falls on a downstroke; the very last note of bar 2 is on an upstroke. The hand leans up a fret for the little finger.
strings.exercise.sixteenth-chug.sixteenth-riff.c: After the take I'll say how even it was and whether the notes were the written ones.
strings.exercise.sixteenth-chug.sixteenth-riff.d: At this speed a real rig's input delay can push notes out of their matching window, which reads as late or missed. Evenness is the number to trust here, and only once the delay is calibrated.
strings.step.triplets-and-bursts.title: Triplets, bursts and tremolo
strings.step.triplets-and-bursts.goal: Chug in triplets, fire a six-note burst into a chord, and tremolo-pick a melody on one string.
strings.step.triplets-and-bursts.why: Three more tools of the fast riff. Triplet chugs are the swing of doom and thrash alike. A burst of sextuplets into a chord is a drum fill on the guitar. Tremolo picking turns a slow melody into a wall of sound. All three depend on a relaxed alternating wrist at speed.
strings.step.triplets-and-bursts.howTo.0: Triplets alternate strictly, so every other beat starts on an upstroke. Accent the first note of each beat either way.
strings.step.triplets-and-bursts.howTo.1: A burst is one flick of six strokes, aimed at the note after it. Rest the hand on the chord.
strings.step.triplets-and-bursts.howTo.2: For tremolo, make the stroke as small as you can and let the wrist stay loose. Tension is what stops it.
strings.step.triplets-and-bursts.payoff: A tremolo-picked melody in E minor, and bursts that land on their chord.
strings.exercise.triplets-and-bursts.triplet-chu: Two bars of muted triplets on the open low E string with the first note of each beat let out.
Count '1-trip-let, 2-trip-let'. Strict down-up, so beats 2 and 4 start on an upstroke.
Make the accent on the upstroke beats as strong as on the downstroke ones.
I check that the first note of each beat was louder, roughly, and how even the triplets were.
At this speed a real rig's input delay can push notes out of their matching window, which reads as late or missed. Evenness is the number to trust here, and only once the delay is calibrated.
Accents are measured roughly, as louder than the notes either side. Compression and high gain flatten them.
strings.exercise.triplets-and-bursts.sextuplet-b: Six muted notes in one beat, then a power chord held for a beat. E, G, E and A.
Sextuplets: six to the click, down-up from a downstroke. The chord lands on the next beat with a downstroke.
Let the hand go soft while the chord rings, and set the fretting hand for the next chord.
I time the six notes and the chord after them. Above the middle rungs, evenness is the number to trust.
At this speed a real rig's input delay can push notes out of their matching window, which reads as late or missed. Evenness is the number to trust here, and only once the delay is calibrated.
On a recording, can you hear six separate notes in each burst?
strings.exercise.triplets-and-bursts.tremolo.pur: A slow E minor melody on the A string with every note picked four times: the melody moves once a beat and the pick never stops.
strings.exercise.triplets-and-bursts.tremolo.how: Sixteenths, strict down-up, no palm mute: let it ring. First finger on fret 7, third on 9, little finger on 10; the hand moves up two frets for bar 2, with the first finger on 9.
Change note exactly on the beat. The fretting hand is slow and the picking hand is fast; don't let one infect the other.
strings.exercise.triplets-and-bursts.tremolo.coa: After the take I'll say how even it was and whether the notes were the written ones.
strings.exercise.triplets-and-bursts.tremolo.det: At this speed a real rig's input delay can push notes out of their matching window, which reads as late or missed. Evenness is the number to trust here, and only once the delay is calibrated.
strings.step.pedal-riffs.title: Pedal-tone riffs
strings.step.pedal-riffs.goal: Play a melody on the A and D strings against a muted open low E, in sixteenths, without the pedal ringing or the melody choking.
strings.step.pedal-riffs.why: A pedal riff is two parts on one guitar: a muted low note that keeps returning and a melody above it. The pick has to leave the low string, cross one or two strings, and come back, in time, and the palm has to mute one string while the other rings.
strings.step.pedal-riffs.howTo.0: Strict alternate picking. The melody notes fall on different strokes as the pattern turns, so don't try to make them all downstrokes.
strings.step.pedal-riffs.howTo.1: Keep the palm on the low E string only. Roll the hand slightly so the A and D strings are free.
strings.step.pedal-riffs.howTo.2: On a skip to the D string, the pick travels over the A string in a small arc. Don't lift the forearm.
strings.step.pedal-riffs.payoff: A riff where a melody on two strings dances over a chugging low E.
strings.exercise.pedal-riffs.pedal-a.title: Melody on the A string
strings.exercise.pedal-riffs.pedal-a.purpose: E, F# and G on the A string, each followed by two muted open E notes: groups of three sixteenths that roll across the beat.
strings.exercise.pedal-riffs.pedal-a.howTo.0: First finger on fret 7, third on 9, little finger on 10. One melody note, two pedal notes.
strings.exercise.pedal-riffs.pedal-a.howTo.1: The melody notes ring and the open E is muted. Keep the strokes alternating through every crossing.
strings.exercise.pedal-riffs.pedal-a.coachLine: After the take I'll say how even it was and whether the notes were the written ones.
strings.exercise.pedal-riffs.pedal-a.detection.0: At this speed a real rig's input delay can push notes out of their matching window, which reads as late or missed. Evenness is the number to trust here, and only once the delay is calibrated.
strings.exercise.pedal-riffs.pedal-a.selfCheck.0: Did the muted notes thud with a clear pitch, neither ringing open nor choked dead?
strings.exercise.pedal-riffs.pedal-skip.title: Melody on the D string
strings.exercise.pedal-riffs.pedal-skip.purpose: The same pattern with the melody a string further away: A, B and C on the D string, and the A string skipped on every crossing.
strings.exercise.pedal-riffs.pedal-skip.howTo.0: The same three fingers on the same frets, one string higher. Rest a spare finger on the A string so it can't ring.
strings.exercise.pedal-riffs.pedal-skip.howTo.1: The skip makes the pick's journey longer. Slow down until the pedal notes are as even as before.
strings.exercise.pedal-riffs.pedal-skip.coachLin: After the take I'll say how even it was and whether the notes were the written ones.
strings.exercise.pedal-riffs.pedal-skip.detectio: At this speed a real rig's input delay can push notes out of their matching window, which reads as late or missed. Evenness is the number to trust here, and only once the delay is calibrated.
strings.exercise.pedal-riffs.pedal-both.title: Melody on both strings
strings.exercise.pedal-riffs.pedal-both.purpose: The melody now jumps between the A and D strings over the same pedal: fifths and sixths in the tune, a crossing and a skip in every beat.
strings.exercise.pedal-riffs.pedal-both.howTo.0: Bar 1 climbs: the A string note, then the same fret on the D string. Bar 2 comes back down.
strings.exercise.pedal-riffs.pedal-both.howTo.1: Keep both fingers of each pair down together, like a small chord, and pick one string at a time.
strings.exercise.pedal-riffs.pedal-both.coachLin: This is the Step's test piece. I'll say how even it was and check the notes after the take.
strings.exercise.pedal-riffs.pedal-both.detectio: At this speed a real rig's input delay can push notes out of their matching window, which reads as late or missed. Evenness is the number to trust here, and only once the delay is calibrated.
strings.step.stop-start.title: Chugs with holes in them
strings.step.stop-start.goal: Play sixteenth-note riffs where some of the sixteenths are silent, so the riff starts and stops inside the beat.
strings.step.stop-start.why: Modern heavy riffs are as much silence as sound: a burst of chugs, a hole, a chord, another hole. The holes are what make it heavy, and they only work if the strings are completely dead in them and the next note comes in exactly on its sixteenth.
strings.step.stop-start.howTo.0: The picking hand swings in sixteenths the whole time, down-up, and only touches the string on the written notes.
strings.step.stop-start.howTo.1: In a rest, the palm presses down a little harder and the fretting hand relaxes on the strings. Nothing rings.
strings.step.stop-start.howTo.2: Count '1 e and a' out loud at the first rung and say the played syllables louder.
strings.step.stop-start.payoff: A stop-start riff that sounds like a machine switching on and off.
strings.exercise.stop-start.chug-rest.title: Two on, one off
strings.exercise.stop-start.chug-rest.purpose: Chug, chug, rest, in sixteenths: a three-sixteenth figure that rolls across the beat, on the muted low E string, with two open eighths to end the second bar.
strings.exercise.stop-start.chug-rest.howTo.0: Count the sixteenths '1 2 3, 1 2 3' and play on 1 and 2. Four times, then three chugs and a rest to fill the bar.
strings.exercise.stop-start.chug-rest.howTo.1: The hand keeps swinging down-up, so the figure starts on a downstroke, then an upstroke, in turn.
strings.exercise.stop-start.chug-rest.coachLine: I time each chug against where it is written. A sound in a rest counts as an extra note.
At this speed a real rig's input delay can push notes out of their matching window, which reads as late or missed. Evenness is the number to trust here, and only once the delay is calibrated.
On a recording, do the stops sound silent, with nothing ringing through them?
strings.exercise.stop-start.chord-and-burst.purp: A power chord on the beat, half a beat of silence, four muted sixteenths, another hole, a chord off the beat. Two bars, E, G and A.
strings.exercise.stop-start.chord-and-burst.howT: Bar 1: E chord on 1, rest, four chugs on beat 2, rest, G chord on the 'and' of 3, two chugs and half a beat of rest.
Kill each chord with both hands. The chugs after a hole start exactly on the beat, not a hair before.
strings.exercise.stop-start.chord-and-burst.coac: I time every attack, chord and chug alike. A chord's pitch is not something I check.
strings.exercise.stop-start.chord-and-burst.dete: At this speed a real rig's input delay can push notes out of their matching window, which reads as late or missed. Evenness is the number to trust here, and only once the delay is calibrated.
strings.exercise.stop-start.chord-and-burst.self: On a recording, do the stops sound silent, with nothing ringing through them?
strings.exercise.stop-start.gallop-holes.title: A gallop with holes
strings.exercise.stop-start.gallop-holes.purpose: A gallop, then sixteenths with the first and last one missing, then open notes on frets 3, 5 and 6 with a single chug between them. E blues on one string.
strings.exercise.stop-start.gallop-holes.howTo.0: Bar 1: '1, and a, (2) e and, 3, a, 4'. The open notes on frets 3 and 5 are eighths; the single chug before beat 4 is on the 'a'.
strings.exercise.stop-start.gallop-holes.howTo.1: First finger on fret 3, third on 5, little finger on 6. Let the hand lean up a fret for the little finger.
strings.exercise.stop-start.gallop-holes.coachLi: This is the Step's test piece. I'll say how even it was and check the notes after the take.
strings.exercise.stop-start.gallop-holes.detecti: At this speed a real rig's input delay can push notes out of their matching window, which reads as late or missed. Evenness is the number to trust here, and only once the delay is calibrated.
strings.step.riffs-at-length.title: The band, and a full minute
strings.step.riffs-at-length.goal: Hold a galloping riff over a rock band for four bars, and keep downstrokes and gallops going for sixty seconds.
strings.step.riffs-at-length.why: A riff is played for minutes, not bars. Downpicking at speed is a stamina skill, the picking arm tires long before the fingers do, and the first sign is the time drifting late. A band behind you makes the same demand a different way: the riff has to lock to the kick drum.
strings.step.riffs-at-length.howTo.0: For the minute-long takes, choose a rung about 20% below your clean tempo. It should feel easy for the first ten seconds.
strings.step.riffs-at-length.howTo.1: Keep the shoulder down and the grip on the pick light. If the forearm locks, the set is over.
strings.step.riffs-at-length.howTo.2: Stop at any pain in the hand, wrist or forearm. A tired forearm is one thing and pain is another; pain ends the set.
strings.step.riffs-at-length.payoff: A four-bar riff that sits on a band, and a minute of downstrokes that ends as tight as it began.
strings.exercise.riffs-at-length.band-riff.title: A riff with the band
strings.exercise.riffs-at-length.band-riff.purpo: Four bars in E minor over a hard rock groove: gallops on E with a climbing answer, then the gallop moved to G and to A.
strings.exercise.riffs-at-length.band-riff.howTo: Bars 1 and 2 are on the open low E string, with answers on frets 3, 5 and 6. Bar 3 gallops on fret 3, muted, and bar 4 on the open A string.
Listen to the kick drum. Your long notes land with it.
strings.exercise.riffs-at-length.band-riff.coach: Band on. I time your notes against it and check them after the take. Direct input or headphones make that fair.
strings.exercise.riffs-at-length.band-riff.detec: With a microphone and speakers the band reaches the same input as you. Direct input or headphones are the honest way to grade this; without them it is untested.
At this speed a real rig's input delay can push notes out of their matching window, which reads as late or missed. Evenness is the number to trust here, and only once the delay is calibrated.
strings.exercise.riffs-at-length.down-minute.pur: Muted eighths on the low E string, every one a downstroke, for sixty seconds. The classic thrash endurance test, at a tempo you choose.
strings.exercise.riffs-at-length.down-minute.how: Eighth notes, all down, with frets 3 and 5 at the end of each bar to mark it.
When it starts to burn, make the stroke smaller before you slow down. If it still burns, stop.
strings.exercise.riffs-at-length.down-minute.coa: I check that the time holds to the end of the minute. Whether every stroke was down is yours to say.
strings.exercise.riffs-at-length.down-minute.det: At this speed a real rig's input delay can push notes out of their matching window, which reads as late or missed. Evenness is the number to trust here, and only once the delay is calibrated.

Long unbroken playing, especially high-gain, can drown out where each note starts, so the app may stop hearing you. Unproven either way; if the app says it did not catch enough, believe that before you doubt your hands.
strings.exercise.riffs-at-length.down-minute.sel: Were they all downstrokes, to the last bar?
strings.exercise.riffs-at-length.gallop-minute.p: The gallop on the low E string for sixty seconds, with a fretted gallop at the end of each bar.
strings.exercise.riffs-at-length.gallop-minute.h: Down, down-up, without a break. The two short notes are the first thing to blur when the arm tires.
Breathe, and drop the shoulder at a bar line if it has crept up.
strings.exercise.riffs-at-length.gallop-minute.c: I check that the time holds to the end of the minute and that the short notes are still there.
strings.exercise.riffs-at-length.gallop-minute.d: At this speed a real rig's input delay can push notes out of their matching window, which reads as late or missed. Evenness is the number to trust here, and only once the delay is calibrated.

strings.level.beginner.title: Beginner: the chug
strings.level.beginner.summary: Palm-muted downstrokes, two-note power chords, and the two together in a riff.
strings.level.beginner.startHereIf.0: You can play eighth notes with a click at 80 BPM.
strings.level.beginner.startHereIf.1: You've never practised palm muting, or your muted notes come out uneven.
strings.level.beginner.startHereIf.2: You can't yet change between two power chords in time.
strings.exercise.warmup-beginner.root-chug.title: A chug on the root
strings.exercise.warmup-beginner.root-chug.purpo: Muted eighths on one string: the root and its minor third, then the fourth and fifth a hand higher. A different key and string each time.
strings.exercise.warmup-beginner.root-chug.howTo: Start well under your clean tempo. All downstrokes, palm-muted. The hand moves up five frets at the bar line and back.
strings.exercise.warmup-beginner.root-chug.coach: This is a warm-up. It tells you how it went, and it decides nothing.
strings.level.intermediate.title: Intermediate: the gallop
strings.level.intermediate.summary: The gallop, the reverse gallop, and continuous alternate-picked sixteenths with accents.
strings.level.intermediate.startHereIf.0: You can play palm-muted eighths in downstrokes at 100 BPM, even and all the same weight.
strings.level.intermediate.startHereIf.1: You can change between E, G and A power chords in eighth notes.
strings.level.intermediate.startHereIf.2: Your gallops smear, or you can't switch between a gallop and straight sixteenths.
strings.exercise.warmup-intermediate.root-gallop: The gallop on one string: the root and its minor third, then the fourth and fifth a hand higher. A different key and string each time.
Start well under your clean tempo. Down, down-up, palm-muted. The hand moves up five frets at the bar line and back.
This is a warm-up. It tells you how it went, and it decides nothing.
strings.level.advanced.title: Advanced: speed and stamina
strings.level.advanced.summary: Triplet chugs, sextuplet bursts and tremolo picking, pedal-tone riffs across strings, stop-start riffs with silent sixteenths, then a riff over a band and a full minute.
strings.level.advanced.startHereIf.0: You can play the gallop and the reverse gallop evenly at 100 BPM.
strings.level.advanced.startHereIf.1: You can alternate-pick muted sixteenths at 95 BPM with an accent on each beat.
strings.level.advanced.startHereIf.2: Your riffs fall apart when they leave the low string, or your picking arm tires before a song is over.
strings.exercise.warmup-advanced.root-sixteenths: Four muted sixteenths a note, alternate picked: the root and its minor third, then the fourth and fifth a hand higher. A different key and string each time.
Start well under your clean tempo. Strict down-up, palm-muted. The hand moves up five frets at the bar line and back.
This is a warm-up. It tells you how it went, and it decides nothing.
At this speed a real rig's input delay can push notes out of their matching window, which reads as late or missed. Evenness is the number to trust here, and only once the delay is calibrated.
